2. Facts in short are that: The Petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.319 of 1983 in the Court of Sadar Munsif, Shariatpur for declaration of title and khas possession in respect of .92 acres of land of C.S. Plot N.63 appertaining to C.S. Khatian no. .25 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 63 appertaining to C.S. khatian no. 25 within C.S. Mouza No.128 Hajotkhola, P.S. Palong, District Faridpur now Shariatpur which has been recorded during R.S. operation in Plot Nos. 90-94 of knatian no. 38-40 alleging inter alia that the suit joma originally belonged to Sari Mohammad and others from the legal heirs of whom Abdul Hamid Munshi purchased 1/3rd share of the joma to the plaintiff No.4, Reazuddin Saiyal being owner in possession of the 1/3rd lnad of the Joma left the plaintiff petitioner no.1 and Altazuddin being owner of 1/3rd share died leaving the defendants no.3 and 4 as heirs. The plaintiff came to know that the S.A. and R.S. khatian have been wrongly prepared and as such the defendant No.10.12 on the basis of the said wrong record dispossessed the plaintiff in respect of a part of the suit land towards the last part of Baiskh for which the plaintiff brought the present suit for declaration of title and for khas possession. 

 and came to a finding upon every issues in favour of the plaintiff and as such decreed the suit on contest against the defendant Nos. 1-5 and also decreed for eviction of the defendant no.10 and khas possession of the plaintiff by his judgment and decree dated 29.11.86. 

 8. Mr. Khan then submits that the learned lower appellate Court committed illegality in reversing the judgment and decree of the trial court for declaration of title and confirmation of khas possession in respect of .92 decimals of land without assigning any sufficient and cognent reason with respect to possession trial Court upon recording evidence of P.Ws. and D.Ws and upon discussion of the evidences and other materials on record come to the conclusion that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit land. The learned Advocate, therefore, submits that the appellate Court has reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court without adverting to this finding of possession made by the trial court as such the judgment of reversal is not a proper judgment and the same cannot stand which should be set aside.
